lesson.title: Er Gym
lesson.subtitle: er is, er zijn, er van, er mee — the four jobs of er in one drill

hook.title: Where Is Er?
hook.content: Er can stand alone or fuse with a preposition. Er is een boek, ik ben er, ik heb er twee, ik ga er mee. The job changes; the word stays small.

pattern.title: Er before the preposition or after the verb
pattern.content: Alone, er follows the verb or introduces existence: ik ben er, er is water. With a preposition it fuses: ermee, ervan, erop. The fusion is optional in speech but common.
pattern.trap_note: Do not confuse er (unstressed there) with daar (stressed there). Daar points; er structures.

exercises.prompt: Match each English meaning with its Dutch twin (Er Gym):
exercises.target_answer: er, hier, daar, mee, van, op
exercises.meaning: there; of it/them, here, there, along; with, of, from, on
exercises.explanation: These are the anchors of "Er Gym": read each Dutch form through the pattern, not as a new word.
“Ik ben er.” is the Dutch form; the other readings bend the pattern of “Er Gym”.

cues: The pattern: Er before the preposition or after the verb
exercises.explanation: “Er is water.” puts the thought together the Dutch way — Er before the preposition or after the verb.

diagnosis.slip: an English-shaped word order slipped in
diagnosis.cue: Do not confuse er (unstressed there) with daar (stressed there). Daar points; er structures.

exercises.prompt: Which English sentence is built the Dutch way?
exercises.explanation: “Ik heb er twee.” is word-for-word “I have there two.”. The odd English is the lesson — never a model to produce. Pattern: Er before the preposition or after the verb.

exercises.prompt: Listen and write the whole sentence.
cues: It means: I am going with it.
exercises.explanation: “Ik ga er mee.” reuses only material taught in “Er Gym” — Er before the preposition or after the verb.
exercises.affirmation: You heard “Ik ga er mee.” — a sentence built from the lesson's own Dutch, practising Er before the preposition or after the verb.

twist.prompt: One more, no safety net — say: “We are there.”
twist.explanation: Er follows the finite verb and covers the location.

summary.outcome: Use er alone and fused with prepositions.
summary.takeaway: Er is a structural pronoun: it points to existence, place or quantity without naming it.
summary.curiosity_teaser: Up next on De Brug: Subordinate Clauses.

er.etymology_derivation: The unstressed 'there' pronoun, with existential, locative and partitive jobs.

hier.etymology_derivation: The same place word as English here.

daar.etymology_derivation: The same place word as English there; the d is the old th.

mee.etymology_derivation: The separable particle in meebrengen and the fixed phrase met ... mee.

van.etymology_derivation: English of and off are the same family; Dutch keeps the v.

op.context_translation: The book is on the table.
op.etymology_derivation: English up and on both lie behind this little word.
